scope: Black Liberation Front: distinguish Pennsylvania prison organizing from East Palo Alto activism; three missing people with actual extended custody.

elijah.label: Jill Soffiyah Elijah, New Afrikan/Black Political Prisoners and Prisoners of War: Conditions of Confinement, p.5. Undated research-committee paper describes Pennsylvania Black Liberation Front prison organizing and reports Clifford Lumumba Futch’s fourteen years in a control unit. Political-retaliation explanation attributed to the author.

ford.label: Ford v. Beister, Civil No.80-0992 (M.D.Pa. April 16, 1986), memorandum and order, discussion. Actual SCI Dallas segregation, March 1980 placement, religious-services and other prison-rights claims; officials’ security rationale and mixed procedural outcome.

futch1976.label: Commonwealth v. Futch, 469 Pa.422, 366 A.2d246 (November 24, 1976). Reversed death judgment and ordered retrial because requested questions about witness-status bias were excluded; did not find that refusal of racial-bias questions required reversal.

loquist.label: Bill Lofquist, SUNY Geneseo sociologist, Clifford B. Futch, published February 12, 2018, updated February 25, 2022. Reports acquittal October 10, 1981, citing Pittsburgh Post-Gazette October 12, 1981; later separate convictions explain why acquittal did not establish release. Its account of the 1976 reversal is corrected against the opinion.

workers1980.label: Workers Viewpoint, March 8, 1980, p.2, Prisoner Prosecuted for Klansman’s Death. Contemporary movement report links Clifford Lumumba Futch’s name to the Ganss prosecution and describes solitary confinement. Its depiction of the victim and political motive is attributed, not adopted as a court finding.

pamoja_may.label: Pamoja Venceremos, no.1, May 18, 1971, p.3, Pigs Invade Brother’s Home. Contemporary account of May 4 arrests; Keith later bailed out, Renard still jailed at publication. Scan visually checked. Claims of police brutality are the publication’s account.

pamoja_july.label: Pamoja Venceremos, no.4, July 2, 1971, pp.12–13, Another BLF Brother Busted. June 24 sentencing: Keith four months, Renard five; both described as incarcerated with a request to visit them in county jail. Distinguishes Keith’s separate June 23–24 overnight detention. Scan visually checked.

prisoner.name: Clifford “Lumumba” Futch
prisoner.aka: Clifford Futch; Clifford B. Futch; Lumumba Futch
prisoner.description: Clifford “Lumumba” Futch was a Pennsylvania prisoner associated with Black Liberation Front prison organizing for religious freedom and humane treatment, according to lawyer Jill Soffiyah Elijah. She reports fourteen years in a control unit. His prison-rights litigation challenged restrictions at SCI Dallas. A separate death sentence was reversed in 1976; scholar Bill Lofquist reports his acquittal in that prosecution in 1981. That acquittal did not resolve his other convictions. His later custody status and vital dates remain unverified.

cases.charges: Administrative segregation and prison-rights restrictions challenged in Ford v. Beister
cases.sentence: Elijah reports fourteen years in a control unit and interprets the treatment as repression of prison organizing. The 1986 court opinion independently documents long-term restricted housing at SCI Dallas, a March 1980 placement, and claims concerning religious services, reviews and other restrictions. Officials cited security concerns. Most challenged claims were dismissed; the religious-services issue was remanded for further consideration. This record describes administrative confinement, not a new fourteen-year criminal sentence. The exact isolation endpoints and total continuous time served are not established.

entries.custody_evidence: Lawyer’s named fourteen-year control-unit account is independently corroborated as extended restricted custody by the 1986 federal civil-rights opinion.

case_research.custody_evidence: Actual extended administrative confinement in Pennsylvania. Political interpretation and security rationale are distinguished. Earlier nonpolitical convictions are not entered as activism cases; no isolation start or end is fabricated.

entries.status_research: Later status unresolved. Neither current imprisonment, release nor death is asserted. Both non-null status flags false use the existing Other category; no ongoing custody counter.

prisoner.name: Keith King
prisoner.description: Keith King was an East Palo Alto Black Liberation Front member. Pamoja Venceremos reported his May 4, 1971 arrest with his brother Renard and a four-month jail sentence on June 24. Its July 2 issue confirms both brothers were jailed and presents their case as political repression. Their exact release dates are unverified.

cases.charges: May 4, 1971 confrontation with San Mateo County deputies; exact statutory counts unverified
cases.convicted: No-contest plea reported; request to withdraw denied
cases.sentence: Four months, imposed June 24, 1971. The July 2 report confirms custody. Keith’s separate overnight traffic detention is not the basis for inclusion. Full time served remains unknown.

entries.custody_evidence: July 2 report describes jail after June 24 sentencing, beyond overnight detention.

case_research.custody_evidence: May arrest and later sentenced custody. Keith had intervening bail; no continuous May–July interval is entered.

prisoner.name: Renard King
prisoner.description: Renard King was jailed with his brother Keith in a 1971 East Palo Alto case supported by the Black Liberation Front. Contemporary accounts describe resistance to police mistreatment and place him in custody after the May 4 arrest and June 24 sentencing. Formal BLF membership is not established.

cases.charges: May 4, 1971 confrontation with San Mateo County deputies; exact statutory counts unverified
cases.convicted: Guilty plea reported; request to withdraw denied
cases.sentence: Five months, imposed June 24, 1971. The May 18 issue already described Renard as still jailed following the May 4 arrest; the July 2 report confirms later custody. Release and full time served are unverified.

research_notes: New missing profiles only; preserve every existing identity and its full data. All source URLs remain research references, never personal support websites. Unknown vital dates and photographs left blank. Approximate community coordinates, not exact premises. No incarceration-start, release date or numeric time-served field; sentence lengths and historical report of control-unit years are not converted into exact counters. Unknown later status explicitly retained. Renard is linked to the broader Black Liberation Movement, not asserted a formal BLF member. County jail is named in case context without substituting an unmatched institution. Existing Leo Hazzile/Bazile spelling issue flagged in audit, not edited or duplicated.
